name: Executive order of April 19, 1879 setting apart the Columbia (Moses) Reservation
nations: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation (Chief Moses' people: Columbia (Sinkiuse), Chelan, Entiat and Wenatchi)
promises: The Indian Claims Commission summarises the order as setting apart the Columbia Reservation for the permanent use and occupancy of Chief Moses and his people, and other friendly Indians who settled there with his consent and the Secretary of the Interior's.
Royce records later orders adding to the reservation (March 6, 1880) and restoring a northern strip along the British Columbia line to the public domain.
today: Under an agreement of July 7, 1883, ratified by the Act of July 4, 1884 (23 Stat. 76, 79-80), Moses' people gave up the Columbia Reservation in return for a promise of equal rights on the Colville Reservation; except for allotted tracts it was restored to the public domain by executive order of May 1, 1886 (ICC findings, 1967). The Colville Tribes' claim in Docket 181-A, that moving Moses' groups onto the Colville Reservation took an interest in Colville lands without compensation, was settled by compromise together with Docket 181-B for a net judgment of $3,500,000.00 in 1967, with no finding of liability.

nationVoice.nation: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation
nationVoice.summary: The Colville Tribes' fish and wildlife program records that the Columbia Reservation was set aside in 1879 for Chief Moses and his people, who included Wenatchi, Chelan and Entiat, and that his people were moved to the Colville Reservation from 1886.

openQuestions: treaties.json lists the present-day tribe as the Nez Perce Tribe of Idaho. Chief Moses' people (Columbia or Sinkiuse, Chelan, Entiat, Wenatchi) are today part of the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation; the Nez Perce link appears to come from Royce's tribe column and looks wrong.
Royce area 659 (the allotments to Sar-sarp-kin and his band confirmed in 1886) belongs with the May 1, 1886 record rather than this one.

No Indian Claims Commission or court finding on the loss of the Columbia Reservation itself was located. Dockets 222 and 224 (Colville for the Moses Band) concerned aboriginal lands found taken on March 8, 1859 under the Yakima treaty, and were settled in 1965; that is a different event.
The text of the 1879 order was not opened; the summary of it is the Commission's and Royce's.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Court of Claims "Moses", "Columbia" and "Colville" (no case about the Columbia Reservation) and ICC full text "Moses Columbia reservation 1879", "Columbia reservation Moses 1884" (opened Yakima Docket 161 and Colville Docket 224 decisions, OSU 214 and 276, which recount the reservation as background); nothing new.
